hints: Water above a position is limited by the shorter of the tallest bars to its left and right.
Try maintaining a left maximum and right maximum while moving two pointers inward.
When the current left height is smaller, the left side can be resolved using the left maximum; otherwise resolve the right side.
title: Trapping Rain Water Problem

notes: The returned value is the total number of trapped water units; each bar has width 1.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units because the lower boundary around each interior position determines its water level.
The lower boundary formed by the surrounding bars results in 9 total units of trapped water.

content.problemStatement: You receive `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is `1`, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

notes: Inputs are valid JSON argument arrays; the only argument is the integer array `height`.
The maximum possible answer under the stated constraints fits in a signed 32-bit integer: (n-2) * 10^5 <= 1,999,800,000.
solution.approach: Use two pointers. At each step, process the side with the smaller current boundary because its trapped level is determined by that side’s maximum seen so far. Maintain leftMax and rightMax and accumulate the difference between the applicable boundary and the current bar.

better.description: Precompute prefix maximums from the left and suffix maximums from the right, then compute the water above every position in one pass.

optimal.description: Use two pointers and maintain the maximum boundary seen from each side. Process the side with the smaller current height; its water level is already determined by the corresponding side maximum.

bruteForce.description: For each position, scan left and right to find the highest boundary on both sides. The water above that position is max(0, min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[i]).

followUps: Can you solve it using prefix/suffix maximum arrays?
Can you solve it with a monotonic stack?
Can you explain why the two-pointer method needs only O(1) auxiliary space?
learningObjectives: Recognize when two-pointer boundary reasoning can replace extra arrays.
Understand how left and right maxima determine trapped water.
Compare brute-force, prefix/suffix, stack, and two-pointer approaches.
